title: Which role carries the rules?
options: system
user
assistant
explanation: The system message carries standing instructions such as tone, format or limits for the whole conversation. The user message is the request, and assistant messages are earlier model replies.
hint: Which message holds the instruction that begins with "Answer"?

title: How many messages does the model see?
explanation: Chat completion APIs are stateless. The second request contains one message, so the model cannot know the name. To keep context, resend earlier turns: [...history, assistantReply, newQuestion].
hint: Count the messages inside request2 only.

title: Reading a streamed reply
options: JSON.parse fails because each line starts with "data: " and the last one is [DONE].
The loop is correct. Streams are plain JSON arrays.
The delta property never exists in a stream.
explanation: Server-sent events prefix each payload with "data: " and finish with a literal [DONE] marker. Remove the prefix, stop at [DONE], skip blank lines, then parse the JSON.
hint: Compare the raw line with what JSON.parse expects.

title: A reply that stops mid-sentence
options: The model chose to end the sentence there.
The reply reached the max_tokens limit and was cut off.
The request was blocked by CORS.
explanation: A finish_reason of "length" means the output hit the token limit. Raise max_tokens, shorten the prompt, or ask for a shorter answer.

title: Turning temperature down
code:
a = client.chat(prompt, temperature=0)
b = client.chat(prompt, temperature=1)
# Which statement is the safest to rely on?
options: temperature 0 makes the model slightly more deterministic, but identical output is not guaranteed.
temperature 0 guarantees byte-for-byte identical replies forever.
temperature has no effect on sampling.
explanation: Lower temperature reduces randomness in token sampling, so replies vary less. Hosted models can still change between calls or versions, so do not treat it as a guarantee.
hint: Which word is stronger: "more deterministic" or "guarantees"?

title: A key in front-end code
options: Anyone who opens developer tools can copy the key. Call your own server, which holds the key.
This is safe because browsers hide headers.
The only problem is the missing semicolon.
explanation: Code that ships to a browser can be inspected, including request headers. Keep provider keys on a server you control and let the browser call that server, with your own limits and authentication.
hint: Who can read a page’s network requests?

title: How many chunks?
explanation: The loop starts at 0, 6, 12 and 18. The start at 18 still pushes "st", which is already inside the previous chunk. Real chunkers usually stop once a chunk reaches the end of the text.

title: Similarity of two vectors
code:
a = [1, 0]
b = [0.6, 0.8]
print(sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b)))
explanation: For vectors normalised to length 1, the dot product equals cosine similarity. Here 1*0.6 + 0*0.8 = 0.6. Closer to 1 means more similar direction.

title: Pick the top two
options: b,d
b,c
d,b
explanation: Sorting is descending by score. Array.sort is stable in modern JavaScript, so b and d keep their original order when scores tie. The first two are b and d.
hint: What happens to equal scores in a stable sort?

title: Different embedding models
code:
doc_vectors = model_a.embed(chunks)
query_vector = model_b.embed(question)
results = nearest(doc_vectors, query_vector)
options: Vectors from different models live in different spaces, so the scores are meaningless. Use the same model for documents and queries.
This is fine. All embeddings are interchangeable.
The only issue is that the chunks are too short.
explanation: Each embedding model defines its own vector space, and sizes can differ. Index and query vectors must come from the same model and settings. Re-embed everything when you switch models.
hint: Can numbers from two different models be compared directly?

title: When nothing matches
options: Add a minimum score. If nothing passes it, say the documents do not cover the question instead of forcing weak context.
Always send more chunks.
Remove the question from the prompt.
explanation: Returning the least-bad chunks encourages the model to answer from irrelevant text. A relevance threshold and an explicit "not found" path make answers more honest.
hint: What should happen when the documents have no answer?

title: Instructions inside a document
options: Treat retrieved text as untrusted data: delimit it clearly, tell the model it is reference material only, and limit what the model can do.
Retrieved text is always safe because it came from your own database.
Hide the problem by lowering the temperature.
explanation: Documents can contain instructions, intentionally or not. Separate them from your rules, label them as quoted material, avoid giving the model powerful tools by default, and review sensitive actions. No wording removes the risk completely.
hint: Who wrote the text inside the retrieved chunk?
